sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less; AES extinct; classification Rai Coast > Greater Yaganon. No descriptive references.

sources.citation: Миклухо-Маклай Н. Н. Собрание сочинений в 6 т., 2-е изд., испр. и доп. Т. 3: Статьи и материалы по антропологии и этнографии народов Океании (отв. ред. Д. Д. Тумаркин, Н. Н. Миклухо-Маклай-мл.). СПб.: Премиум-пресс, 2020. Text 'Список некоторых слов и образцов речи, собранных на Берегу Маклая в 1876—1877 гг.', printed pp. 158-163 (Bai column pp. 161-163), commentary pp. 402-403. [= re-edition from the manuscript AGO F.6 Op.1 No.22 of the list first printed in Собр. соч. Т. 3 Ч. 1, 1951, с. 178-183 = Glottolog ref 312521]
sources.note: Nothing. The Бай (Bai) column is a c. 60-item wordlist (items 1-76 with gaps) in Latin script with no stress/accent marks at all (checked page scan); the only mention of stress in the whole dialect section is editorial footnote 6* to the Bongu list, 'В рукописи далее ударения отсутствуют' (stress marks absent in the manuscript from here on). Editors' note 1 (V. I. Belikov) equates Бай with the language Dumun.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2019. A fragment of Papua New Guinea philology. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 37: 42-60.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for Bai (or Bongu). On Bai: 'Of the 64 items from now extinct Bai, 25 have cognates in other Rai Coast languages.. 16 cognates are in the Yaganon subgroup.. This confirms Pawley & Hammarström's (2018:63) assignment.. of Bai to the Yaganon subgroup.. But the list is too short for an assessment of its accuracy' (p. 44). Phonological content is limited to Maclay's segmental transcription errors in Bongu (n vs ŋ, allophones of /q/, the Cyrillic soft sign for laminal l). Also states that Loukotka 1953 says 'almost nothing.. about the content of Maclay's materials'…

sources.citation: Миклухо-Маклай, Н. Н. 1993. Собрание сочинений в 6 т. Т. 3: Статьи и материалы по антропологии и этнографии народов Океании. М.: Наука. Док. №17 'Список некоторых слов и образцов речи, собранных на Берегу Маклая в 1876-1877 гг.' (Бай column) and №15 'Папуасские диалекты Берега Маклая на Новой Гвинее', with editorial commentary; online transcription at vostlit.info (Восточная литература).
sources.note: No phonology content: bare wordlist without accent marks and no prose on Bai pronunciation. The only stress-related words in the Maclay-Coast documents are the editorial parenthesis in the Bongu men's-names list of №15, 'В рукописи далее ударения отсутствуют' ('from here on the manuscript has no stress marks'), which concerns Bongu personal names, not Bai.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: No stress/accent statement anywhere; Dumun (Bx, the language Bai is equated with) had only a short list and is 'discarded in the remainder of this volume'; Miklukho-Maklaj (1951) cited only as a source of 'words and occasional notes'. Nothing on Bai.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The Languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content for Bai or Dumun; the volume is classification, village lists, populations and lexicostatistics. Text search of the whole volume finds no occurrence of stress/accent/tone/pitch. Relevant sentences: 'The Bai language, a member of the Yaganon Family, is extinct.' (p. 5) and 'Only ten out of twenty-eight Bai words are cognate with Dumun. As a result, Maklal's Bai language appears to be an extinct Yaganon language.' (p. 15).

sources.citation: Miklucho-Maclay, N. von. 1882. Papua-Dialekte der Maclay-Küste in Neu-Guinea (with 'Grammatische Bemerkungen', prepared with Herr Grube). In G. von der Gabelentz & A. B. Meyer, Beiträge zur Kenntniss der melanesischen, mikronesischen und papuanischen Sprachen, 491-510. Leipzig: Hirzel.
sources.note: Covers six other Maclay-Coast varieties only (Gorendu/Bongu/Gumbu, Bogati, Bili-Bili, Mitebog, Englam-Mana, Maragum-Mana); Bai is not included. The 'Grammatische Bemerkungen' give a Lautbestand and pronunciation notes but say nothing about Betonung/accent.
